_note: good.md, none-link.md, gate-good.md, gate-glob-good.md, gate-doc-only.md (a markdown file is not a gate file unless it is owner-only: gate-owner-markdown.md edits a skill and has no Gate changes section), gate-base-rule-good.md and gate-none.md pass. placeholder.md is the shipped PR template, unfilled: its example command and #123 live in comments and must not count. A `<name>.changes.json` beside a body lists what that PR changed; the gate-* cases are read against the harness's gate paths. A sidecar's `globs` are the gate paths the base branch's harness listed: a PR that removes a rule is held to it. One line may name a directory glob (`ci/fixtures/known-bad/p1/**`): it covers the files it matches and nothing else. A sidecar's `links` are the symlinks and submodule links the PR adds, removes or changes: each is a gate change (#149); a sidecar without that list is unreadable. gate-gitattributes.md and gate-gitmodules.md each change one of git's own settings files, which the harness guard counts and no harness rule names (#174), and have no Gate changes section. A `<!--` closed by a `-->` beyond a heading may be a comment or two marks written as text, and the check cannot tell which, nor where a section ends (#189): the body gets that one finding and nothing else in it is read. gate-comment-mark.md has the marks in inline code and every gate file on its own line; gate-swallowed-heading.md has the same marks and names a gate file only in a later section; gate-hidden-section.md wraps its whole Gate changes section in a comment.
